title: Safe-33 closure inventory: drop-in-compatible downstream families and their internal ownership mechanisms
superseded_note: Historical closure inventory bound to head_sha 67ae7f8e and crate 0.0.27. Census, cohort and worklist figures other than the two corrected worklist states below are as-of that HEAD and are retained unchanged; do not read them as the current state. Current mechanism states: ERR-1 SAFETY_DISCHARGED (mechanism-discharge-ERR.json); BIO CONTRACTED (B39/B40 boundaries independently checked, mechanism not discharged); RUNTIME_ALLOC_OWNERSHIP and ASN1_OCSP OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED for the openssh-reachable sites (openssh-mechanisms-reconstructed.json), not SAFETY_DISCHARGED.

state_vocabulary.UNSAFE_OPEN: no ownership work on this mechanism's raw boundary on this branch; the boundary is open
state_vocabulary.OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED: the branch models ownership for (some of) the region with owning types/Drop, but no proof discharges the raw-pointer boundary; a Drop wrapper alone is never discharge
state_vocabulary.SAFETY_DISCHARGED: a per-site safety contract for the boundary is proven (no unexplained reachable site in the mechanism); not claimed by a Drop wrapper alone
state_vocabulary.COMPATIBILITY_CONFIRMED: downstream drop-in build/link (L4) is confirmed against the authority
state_vocabulary.SAFE_COMPATIBLE: the mechanism is SAFETY_DISCHARGED and a functional (L7) result is confirmed for families depending on it
state_vocabulary.BLOCKED: cannot advance (no authority unit / external dependency)

reconstruction.scope: the four RUNTIME_ALLOC_OWNERSHIP sites reachable from the openssh closure (the prompt named 3; the frozen inventory records 4: eng_table.rs:148, runtime/ex_data.rs:239, runtime/ex_data.rs:251, runtime/init.rs:1240)
reconstruction.contract: An owner allocated through the crate's `CRYPTO_*` seam is either a raw-storage handle (`RawCtx`) or a validated handle (`OwnedCtx`); `Drop` is the block's single release, `RawCtx` never runs the destructor body, and `assume_init` is the one validated transition. Callbacks this mechanism installs (lhash hash/compare, ex_data new/free/dup) receive only values the installing module itself placed (lhash) or no argument at all (ex_data no-ops). The allocator seam, the exported symbols and `#[repr(C)]` layouts are unchanged.
reconstruction.allocation_seam: crate::runtime::mem CRYPTO_malloc/CRYPTO_zalloc/CRYPTO_free (src/runtime/mem.rs byte-identical to the pre-subphase tree)

sites.contract: `c` is a live `EnginePile` stored in an ENGINE table's lhash: the only installers are `int_table_check` (creates the table with this hash) and `engine_table_register` (inserts only `RawCtx::<EnginePile>` allocations), and the lhash never passes NULL for a stored element.
established_by: caller: OPENSSL_LH_new/HashFunc invocation; the element set is established by this module's own insert sites (one production site, engine_table_register)

sites.contract: No caller contract: no argument is read. The no-op is now a safe `extern "C" fn`, which coerces to the `unsafe extern "C" fn` slot `Callback::free_func` stores.
established_by: vacuous: the body reads no argument

sites.contract: No caller contract: no argument is read, including the `from_d` slot it answers success for. The no-op is now a safe `extern "C" fn`.
established_by: vacuous: the body reads no argument

sites.contract: `abort` is libc's `void abort(void)`: no argument, no memory access, never returns; the `<stdlib.h>` signature is the ABI contract and the symbol must not be interposed with a different one.
established_by: external ABI contract: libc `<stdlib.h>`; the item carries a contiguous `// SAFETY:` prelude in the working tree (the inventory coordinate 1240 predates that prelude)

relocated: engine_pile_hash/engine_pile_cmp now carry the lhash callback contract and name the module's single production insert site

reconstruction.scope: the seven ASN1_OCSP sites reachable from the openssh closure (ssh and sshd carry the same obligation set)
reconstruction.contract: Every callback this mechanism installs is invoked by a named in-crate caller that supplies a live object of the row's declared item type, borrowed for the call and never adopted, plus a live BIO or a correctly sized output cursor. No site takes ownership across the ABI edge except the documented decoder result (d2i_ocsp_nonce) and the encoder output (i2d_ocsp_nonce), whose ownership transitions are stated on the fn. The allocation seam for the one site that allocates transient storage is the crate's `CRYPTO_*` seam, unchanged.
reconstruction.allocation_seam: crate::runtime::mem CRYPTO_malloc/CRYPTO_free (src/runtime/mem.rs byte-identical to the pre-subphase tree)

sites.contract: No caller contract: the C callback `int (*)(unsigned long, void *)` and its `*mut *mut c_uchar` argument are gone. `traverse_string` now takes an `FnMut`, and `cpy_asc`/`cpy_bmp`/`cpy_univ`/`cpy_utf8` are safe fns over `&mut [u8]` + position, so every write is bounds-checked against the block `ASN1_mbstring_ncopy` allocated.
established_by: type invariant: the output slice is the `outlen`-byte view of the `count = outlen + 1` block the same frame allocated; Rust's slice bounds enforce it

sites.contract: `exts` is a writable `STACK_OF(X509_EXTENSION) *` slot and `val` is NULL or readable for a positive `len`; the `Asn1String` the call builds is a borrowed view over a local buffer that `X509V3_add1_i2d` encodes without adopting.
established_by: caller: OCSP_request_add1_nonce / OCSP_basic_add1_nonce pass the address of their own live extension field (`# Safety` on both exported fns)

sites.contract: `_method` is this row (unread), `in` is the live `OCSP_CRLID` the row's `it` decoder produced (borrowed, not retained), `bp` is a live BIO, and each of `crlUrl`/`crlNum`/`crlTime` is NULL or the decoder's live value.
established_by: caller: X509V3_EXT_print (src/x509/v3_prn.rs), which decodes through `method->it` and passes the live BIO

sites.contract: `a` is a live `ASN1_OCTET_STRING` borrowed for the call; `pp` is NULL (size query) or `*pp` is a writable cursor with room for the returned length.
established_by: caller: do_ext_i2d (src/x509/v3_conf.rs) sizes with a NULL destination, allocates `len`, then passes `&mut p` into that block (`# Safety` names the twice-pass encoder contract)

sites.contract: `a` is NULL or a live `ASN1_OCTET_STRING *` slot; `*pp` is readable for `length` bytes with `0 <= length <= c_int::MAX`; on success the caller owns the decoded value, on failure a caller-supplied value is untouched and nothing allocated is leaked.
established_by: caller: X509V3_EXT_d2i / X509V3_EXT_print pass a NULL slot and the extension's own value bytes

sites.contract: No caller contract: every argument is unread. The item is now a safe `extern "C" fn`, which coerces to the row's `unsafe extern "C" fn` slot; the returned `ASN1_NULL` is the caller's.
established_by: vacuous: the body reads no argument

sites.contract: `_method` is this row (unread), `in` is the live `OCSP_SERVICELOC` the row's `it` decoder produced (borrowed, not retained), `bp` is a live BIO, and `issuer`/`locator` are the decoder's own borrowed members.

mechanisms.scope: Definitions of `unsafe extern "C" fn` callbacks, `unsafe extern "C" {}` shim blocks, and internal `unsafe fn` adapters whose caller contract is a raw C/ABI contract rather than an ownership interior. Cross-cutting ABI-edge mechanism: it is not an ownership reconstruction and it does not own the data those callbacks operate on.
mechanisms.discharge_requirement: For each site, a `# Safety` contract naming the caller, the pointer/alias/initialisation preconditions that caller must establish, and the caller-closure evidence that establishes them, reviewed at BOUNDARY. No ownership receipt in another mechanism discharges an ABI-edge function contract.
mechanisms.note: Introduced 2026-10-25 to classify the 11 reachable function-level contract gaps in the openssh closure that no ownership mechanism owns. State is UNSAFE_OPEN: no reconstruction exists yet.

obligation_mechanisms.basis: `cb` is the X509_STORE_set_verify_cb callback. The caller that establishes `ctx` liveness and type is the crypto/x509 store-context verifier, which X509_VERIFY_POLICY owns. Existing mechanism, OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED; its receipt does not enumerate this consumer-side app callback, so no discharge is implied.

Declarations of the C-side ucontext_t shim in src/async/arch/async_ucontext.c. Layout, size and alignment stay on the C side of the ABI; no existing ownership mechanism covers a platform shim and the same-file allocator/lock sites belong to other mechanisms. Classified at the ABI edge, not as async-stack ownership.

`add_error_data_pathbyaddr` is the ERR_add_error_data adapter: its unsafe obligations are the libc `dlerror()` string and `openssl_rs_err_add_data` append, both ERR-owned. ERR-1 is SAFETY_DISCHARGED at mechanism scope but its declared surface does not name this site, so the adjudicator must return UNKNOWN rather than DISCHARGED.

`dynamic_finish` is an ENGINE method callback installed through the ENGINE finish-function slot. No ENGINE ownership mechanism exists in the registry, and an ENGINE ownership reconstruction would not by itself state this callback's caller contract.

`engine_pile_hash` is the OPENSSL_LH_new hash callback over a stored ENGINE_PILE. The lhash representation and callback-invocation contract are in crypto/lhash, which RUNTIME_ALLOC_OWNERSHIP declares. Mechanism state is UNSAFE_OPEN: reconstruction is required before any discharge.
`look_str_cb` is an ENGINE_TABLE_DOALL_CB callback invoked by engine_table_doall under the engine lock. No ENGINE ownership mechanism exists; the obligation is the callback's ABI contract.

`do_ui_passphrase` is an internal `unsafe fn` whose raw-pointer caller contract (pass/pass_len writability, prompt_info NUL-termination, ui_method validity) is documented only at block level. It is a UI/passphrase ABI-edge helper, not an ownership interior; its secret buffers are separately owned by the allocator seam.

`ssl_module_free_thunk` is the CONF_module_add finish callback. The CONF module-registry callback contract is an ABI edge; no CONF ownership mechanism exists. The existing B7-CONF-2 receipt covers the diagnostic builders, not this thunk.
`ui_new_method_data` is a CRYPTO_EX_new callback; the ex-data machinery calls it through a function pointer. No UI ownership mechanism exists; classified at the ABI edge.

`ui_dup_method_data` is a CRYPTO_EX_dup callback that receives and replaces the ex-data slot pointer. Its pointer-to-pointer contract is the ex-data ABI edge, not an ownership interior owned by an existing mechanism.
`ui_close` is a UI_METHOD close callback installed on the wrapper method. No UI ownership mechanism exists; the obligation is the method-table callback contract.

`dummy_psk` is the callback installed by the ciphers app's `SSL_CTX_set_psk_client_callback` (`src/apps/ciphers.rs:271-275`). Its body reads no argument and returns 0, so the caller contract is the PSK client callback ABI and imposes no pointer requirement. C_ABI_CONTRACT's declared authority prefix `apps/` covers app-side C callbacks; no ownership mechanism owns it.
